This is 老地 — I have worked it for 35 years. I do not read, I do not go to meetings. I watch what my neighbors do and I remember what worked last year. My daughter is in the city, so it is just me and my husband. He helps in the busy times.

I have about 10 mu. I do wheat-maize on about 7 mu — that is the good flat land near the canal. On the other 3 mu, the soil is a bit sandier and I plant cotton, like I have done most years. Cotton is more work but the price can be good, and I have seed from my neighbor's cousin who sells it.

**Wheat** — I plant in October after the maize comes off. I use the improved seed the village shop sells, one bag for my land (about 15 kg per mu, I sow a little thick because the weather can be bad). For fertilizer I put 2 bags of the compound (the 15-15-15, 100 jin bags) at planting — that is my base. Then in spring when the wheat greens up, I put 1 bag of urea per mu as topdressing. I water at planting, once in winter if it is dry, once at jointing, and once at filling — that is about 3-4 times from the well. I spray once for aphids, maybe twice if they are bad. I plough with the tractor before planting because the maize stubble is thick. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, I hope for the same.

**Maize** — Right after wheat harvest in June I put the seed in, no ploughing, just push it into the stubble. Hybrid seed, whatever the shop has that the neighbors say is good. I put 1.5 bags of compound as starter and then 1 bag of urea when it is knee-high. Water twice if the rain is poor. Spray once for the borer worm. I usually get around 500 kg per mu.

**Cotton** — This is the harder crop. I plough the land in spring, put 1 bag of compound per mu before planting. I use improved seed. I water at planting and twice more in summer. The bollworm is the problem — I spray 4 or 5 times through the summer, that is just how it is. I put a little urea when the bolls are forming. Last year I got about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu, the year before was worse because of the rain.

I do not want to change much. Fertilizer is expensive but running short is worse — a bad harvest means no money. Better to put a bit extra.
